title: On-device retrieval ships built-in by default in a local-LLM runtime by Q1 2027
body: A widely used local-LLM runtime or RAG framework that runs entirely on-device will ship built-in embedding-and-retrieval as a first-class, default component, so that a user can index documents and run grounded search without ever calling a server-side embedding API. The catalyst is that the historically missing piece for fully local RAG was a small, permissively licensed, genuinely fast multilingual retriever, and Liquid AI's 350M LFM2.5-Embedding and LFM2.5-ColBERT pair, distributed as GGUF builds that run under llama.cpp at sub-10ms query latency on a laptop, removes that bottleneck. Once a retriever this size runs in the same inference stack as the generator and under the same permissive terms, the engineering distance to bundling it as a turnkey 'index-and-ask-your-files' feature collapses. The concrete falsifiable claim: at least one mainstream local runtime or desktop RAG tool (for example a llama.cpp-based app, an Ollama-style runtime, or a comparable local stack) will ship on-device embedding plus retrieval as a documented, default-on capability, with no required external embedding service, by the first quarter of 2027. This would mark on-device retrieval shifting from a hand-wired add-on to standard infrastructure for the local-LLM ecosystem.

reasoning.because: A 350M multilingual retriever now runs under llama.cpp at sub-10ms latency on a laptop CPU/GPU
reasoning.given: Local-LLM stacks want grounded search but avoid server-side embedding calls for privacy and offline
reasoning.so_that: A mainstream local runtime can bundle embedding+retrieval as a default, turnkey on-device RAG feature
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027 a named local-LLM runtime ships built-in on-device retrieval
reasoning.plain_language: Soon a popular offline AI app will search your own files by itself, with no need to send them to any server.

summary: Small, fast, openly licensed retrievers like Liquid AI's 350M LFM2.5 pair remove the last bottleneck for fully local RAG. The prediction: a mainstream local-LLM runtime or desktop RAG tool ships built-in on-device embedding and retrieval as a default, with no server-side embedding call, by Q1 2027.
